articles.title: Homem morre afogado no Poção Azul, entre Uberlândia e Araguari | G1
articles.standfirst: Uma testemunha passava pelo local e viu o homem entrando na água e depois não conseguiu sair. Após ser retirado da água pelo Corpo de Bombeiros, o Samu tentou reanimação por uma hora, mas a morte foi confirmada ainda no local.
articles.summary: Afogamento no Poção Azul mobilizou Bombeiros e Samu após homem de 37 anos entrar em trecho proibido do Rio Uberabinha, entre Uberlândia e Araguari.
articles.body:
Um homem de 37 anos morreu afogado no Poção Azul, trecho do Rio Uberabinha localizado entre Uberlândia e Araguari , próximo à BR-050. O corpo foi retirado da água pelo Corpo de Bombeiros, e apesar da tentativa de reanimação pela equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), o óbito foi declarado no local.

Segundo os bombeiros, o homem entrou na água em uma área particular onde o acesso é proibido. Uma testemunha que passava de bicicleta pelo local viu quando ele entrou no rio e percebeu que não conseguia sair da água. Ela acionou o resgate.

Os bombeiros chegaram ao local e retiraram o homem da água em cerca de oito minutos após o recebimento da chamada. Em seguida, o Samu foi acionado e iniciou as manobras de reanimação, conforme o protocolo de atendimento a vítimas de afogamento, por cerca de uma hora.

Até a última atualização dessa reportagem, a vítima ainda não havia sido identificada.

De acordo com um levantamento do Corpo de Bombeiros, desde 2010, foram registradas 11 pessoas mortes no Poção Azul. Na Cachoeira de Sucupira, que também faz parte do leito do Rio Uberabinha, foram registradas outras 16 mortes no mesmo período, totalizando 27 vítimas nos dois locais.

Nos últimos 15 dias, quatro pessoas morreram afogadas em Uberlândia, segundo a reportagem.

Os bombeiros orientam que as pessoas evitem entrar em locais proibidos para banho e não se arrisquem em rios e cachoeiras. Mesmo quando a água parece tranquila, há riscos de afogamento. A recomendação é permanecer em áreas seguras, próximas à margem, e respeitar a sinalização.

articles.title: What will Lula’s fourth term mean for Brazil?

articles.body:
Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva delivered a defiant message after being declared the winner of a run-off vote on Sunday.

He lost round one to his right-wing rival. But he made history by coming out on top in the second poll.

Opponent Flavio Bolsonaro has disputed the result and says he wants it annulled.

This will be Lula’s fourth nonconsecutive term in office. He’s promised a new approach to governing. But many challenges lie ahead. So, how will his government handle them?

articles.title: Marcha da apuração tem duas viradas e termina com a maior votação já registrada para um candidato à Presidência | G1
articles.standfirst: A participação maior do eleitorado é um dos fatores que ajudam a explicar a vitória de Lula.
articles.summary: A participação maior do eleitorado é um dos fatores que ajudam a explicar a vitória de Lula.
articles.body:
A marcha da apuração teve duas viradas e terminou com a maior votação já registrada para um candidato à Presidência da República. A participação maior do eleitorado é um dos fatores que ajudam a explicar o resultado.

A votação acabou às 19h. A apuração durou exatamente duas horas e quatro minutos. Lula abriu na liderança. Às 19h44, Flávio Bolsonaro passou à frente. O candidato do PL ficou 40 minutos em primeiro lugar e voltou a ser superado por Lula às 20h24. O petista se manteve à frente até a vitória. Às 21h08 veio a confirmação da virada:

“Nós temos agora a definição de presidente da República. Candidato Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, do PT , reeleito presidente da República do Brasil com 51,74% dos votos. Candidato Lula vai governar o país por mais quatro anos, a quarta vez em que ele vai governar o país”.

No segundo turno, Lula teve a maior votação já registrada para um candidato à Presidência da República. Ultrapassou 64,2 milhões votos. Flávio Bolsonaro, que havia liderado a disputa no primeiro turno, recebeu 59,8 milhões votos. Com 100% das urnas apuradas, Lula foi eleito com 51,79% dos votos válidos. Flávio teve 48,21%. A diferença entre os dois foi de 4,4 milhões votos, o equivalente a 3,58 pontos percentuais.

Em relação ao primeiro turno, Lula ganhou 1 0,3 milhões votos a mais. Já Flávio, só 3,7 milhões a mais. Essa foi uma das grandes surpresas da apuração. No primeiro turno, os três outros candidatos de direita - Augusto Cury, Ronaldo Caiado e Renan Santos – receberam, somados, 8,7 milhões votos. Os números mostram que a maioria destes votos não foi transferida para Flávio Bolsonaro, como podia se esperar por serem do mesmo campo político.

Marcha da apuração tem duas viradas e termina com a maior votação já registrada para um candidato à Presidência — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Lula venceu a votação em 13 estados. Em outros 13 e no Distrito Federal, Flávio Bolsonaro teve mais votos. Mas, na comparação com o primeiro turno, em todos os 26 estados e no Distrito Federal, Lula ampliou a votação em um montante maior do que Flávio. E, em seis estados, mais uma surpresa: Flávio teve menos votos no segundo turno do que no primeiro - Acre, Amazonas, Amapá, Roraima, Tocantins e Maranhão. Ou seja, perdeu eleitores de um turno para o outro.

Uma das mudanças mais significativas ocorreu em Minas Gerais, único estado em que Lula virou no segundo turno. O presidente havia ficado atrás de Flávio Bolsonaro no primeiro turno. No domingo (25), conseguiu vencer com 50,43% dos votos. Com isso, Minas Gerais e Amazonas continuam sendo os únicos estados em que o resultado local coincide com o nacional em todas as eleições desde 1989.

Em São Paulo, maior colégio eleitoral do país, a distância a favor de Flávio caiu de 3,4 milhões para 2 milhões de votos entre um turno e outro.

Lula aumentou a votação em todas as regiões. No Sudeste, recebeu 4,8 milhões votos a mais do que no primeiro turno. No Nordeste, Lula teve 2,9 milhões votos a mais.

A maior participação dos eleitores também ajuda a explicar o resultado. No primeiro turno, mais de 33 milhões de eleitores não foram às urnas. No domingo (25), esse número caiu para 30 milhões. Foi o segundo menor índice de abstenção para um segundo turno desde 2006, quando Lula venceu a disputa contra o então concorrente Geraldo Alckmin, à época no PSDB.

Os votos brancos e nulos também caíram do primeiro para o segundo turno: de quase 6 milhões para 4,1 milhões. A tática adotada pela campanha de Lula, na visão do cientista político Murilo Medeiros, teve influência direta no resultado. Houve avanço da participação nas redes sociais e um reforço nas ruas, capazes de sensibilizar os eleitores mais jovens e os mais velhos. Na contagem final, o apoio das mulheres chefes de família das grandes cidades também foi decisivo.

“A mobilização eleitoral nas ruas e no campo digital, atrelada ao discurso do medo, encorajou o brasileiro a sair de casa para votar. Principalmente os idosos e os jovens de baixa renda. Também tem as mulheres, principalmente as que moram nas grandes periferias urbanas das grandes capitais e das grandes cidades brasileiras. É o eleitorado que define o voto mais próximo do dia da eleição, e era uma parcela do eleitorado também mais indecisa e mais sensível a temas concretos, do cotidiano dos brasileiros”, diz Murilo Medeiros, cientista político da Universidade de Brasília.

articles.title: Motorista do PR recebe multa por infração cometida em SP por veículo de modelo e placa diferente do dele | G1
articles.standfirst: DER-SP, que aplicou a multa, disse que o motorista tem direito a recorrer da infração. Órgão não explicou o que pode ter acontecido para levar ao erro.
articles.summary: DER-SP, que aplicou a multa, disse que o motorista tem direito a recorrer da infração. Órgão não explicou o que pode ter acontecido para levar ao erro.
articles.body:
O empresário Edson Lima, morador de Paranaguá , no litoral do Paraná, recebeu uma multa de R$ 130 e quatro pontos na Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) por dirigir 20% acima da velocidade permitida em uma rodovia estadual de Assis , no interior de São Paulo.

O problema é que o carro que cometeu a infração tem outra placa e é de um modelo diferente do carro dele.

A multa recebida por Lima aponta que a infração foi registrada em março deste ano e inclui dados de um veículo Renault registrado em nome do empresário. No entanto, o documento também apresenta uma foto do momento da suposta infração, na qual aparece um carro da marca Toyota.

Inicialmente, Lima achou que poderia se tratar de uma placa clonada e registrou um Boletim de Ocorrência (B.O).

Porém, ao comparar a imagem registrada na autuação com a do próprio carro, ele percebeu que as placas são muito semelhantes: a diferença é que a placa do veículo dele contém a letra "O", enquanto a do carro fotografado traz a letra "D" na mesma posição. Dessa forma, o empresário acredita que a multa tenha sido gerada por um erro na leitura da placa do veículo.

Multa indica descrição do veículo do empresário, mas tem foto de outro carro, com modelo e placa diferente — Foto: Reprodução

A preocupação do empresário é que os quatro pontos previstos na autuação possam resultar na suspensão do direito de dirigir, já que ele corre o risco de atingir o limite de pontos na CNH.

"Você se sente mal, porque, você sabe quando você está errado, você sabe quando você leva uma multa. Agora, essa aqui é uma multa que você fica com aquele medo: se esse carro faz alguma coisa, vamos supor se ele atropela alguém, se ele mata alguém, se ou é usado para algum roubo, alguma coisa, poderia estar sob sobre caindo sobre a minha pessoa", afirma.

Procurado, o Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem do Estado de São Paulo (DER-SP), que aplicou a multa, disse que o motorista tem direito a recorrer da infração. O órgão não explicou o que pode ter acontecido para levar ao erro.

Segundo o Detran Paraná, existem três possibilidades para se defender de autuação por infração de trânsito:

Defesa da autuação: apresentada logo após receber a "Notificação de Autuação", antes da penalidade ser aplicada. Serve para apontar erros formais (dados errados da placa, modelo ou horário);

Recurso Jari: Não havendo apresentação de defesa da autuação ou caso a defesa seja indeferida, a autoridade de trânsito expedirá a notificação da penalidade de multa, indicando o prazo para o cidadão interpor recurso na Junta Administrativa de Recursos e Infrações (Jari). Caso a Defesa Prévia seja negada, você recorre à Jari;

Recurso Cetran: Caso o Recurso Jari seja indeferido, o cidadão será notificado da decisão, podendo interpor Recurso ao Conselho Estadual de Trânsito (Cetran). Este recurso deve ser apresentado até a data estabelecida na notificação do resultado de Recurso Jari. É a última instância administrativa;

É possível apresentar a defesa pela internet , pelos Correios ou presencialmente nas unidades de atendimento do Detran-PR.

articles.title: Aprovação de Trump sobe para 32% após mínima histórica, aponta pesquis | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos mostra que democratas têm vantagem de 11 pontos percentuais nas intenções de voto para o Congresso, que terá sua composição definida em 3 de novembro.
articles.summary: Pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos mostra que democratas têm vantagem de 11 pontos percentuais nas intenções de voto para o Congresso, que terá sua composição definida em 3 de novembro.
articles.body:
A aprovação do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , subiu para 32%, um ponto percentual acima do menor nível registrado na semana anterior, segundo pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos divulgada nesta segunda-feira (26).

O levantamento foi realizado antes das eleições legislativas de 3 de novembro - conhecidas como midterms -, que vão definir os representantes do Congresso dos Estados Unidos. Os republicanos, partido de Trump, tentam manter a maioria na Câmara dos Representantes e no Senado.

Entre os eleitores registrados, 47% disseram preferir candidatos do Partido Democrata, enquanto 36% afirmaram que votariam nos republicanos. Outros 11% disseram não saber em quem votariam se a eleição fosse realizada hoje.

A diferença de 11 pontos percentuais entre os partidos diminuiu um ponto em relação à última pesquisa , encerrada em 19 de outubro.

Quando os eleitores indecisos foram questionados sobre qual partido preferiam, a vantagem dos democratas caiu para nove pontos percentuais. Nesse cenário, os democratas tinham 50% das intenções de voto, contra 41% dos republicanos.

A pesquisa foi realizada pela internet com 1.679 adultos nos Estados Unidos, incluindo 1.280 eleitores registrados. A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais.

Relação com os EUA de Trump será uma das chaves da geopolítica do próximo presidente. — Foto: Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images via BBC

Na semana passada, a aprovação de Trump havia caído para 31%, o menor índice desde o início de seu atual mandato. Na ocasião, 66% dos americanos disseram desaprovar o governo do presidente.

O levantamento, realizado ao longo de quatro dias, também apontou vantagem de 12 pontos percentuais dos democratas sobre os republicanos nas intenções de voto para o Congresso. Os democratas tinham 47% da preferência dos eleitores, contra 35% dos republicanos.

Foi a maior diferença registrada desde o início do atual ciclo eleitoral.

articles.title: Resultado Lotofácil 3074: seis apostas de MT ganham até R$ 6 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogos feitos em seis cidades do estado acertaram 14 dezenas no sorteio desta segunda-feira (26); uma aposta de Poconé levou R$ 6.047,61.
articles.summary: Jogos feitos em seis cidades do estado acertaram 14 dezenas no sorteio desta segunda-feira (26); uma aposta de Poconé levou R$ 6.047,61.
articles.body:
Seis apostas feitas em Mato Grosso ficaram a um número de levar o prêmio principal do concurso 3814 da Lotofácil , sorteado nesta segunda-feira (26). Cada uma acertou 14 das 15 dezenas e ganhou pelo menos R$ 2.015,87.

Os jogos premiados foram registrados em Bom Jesus do Araguaia , Guarantã do Norte , Lambari D’Oeste, Poconé , Porto dos Gaúchos e Poxoréu. Todas as apostas foram simples, sendo uma presencial e cinco feitas pela internet. A aposta de Poconé, com três jogos, recebeu R$ 6.047,61.

Em todo o país, 389 apostas acertaram 14 números e receberam R$ 2.015,87 cada. Duas apostas acertaram as 15 dezenas e ganharam R$ 2.134.251,70 cada. Os jogos foram registrados em Santana (AP) e Belo Horizonte (MG), ambos na modalidade simples e feitos presencialmente.

Os números sorteados foram: 01 – 04 – 06 – 08 – 09 – 12 – 13 – 15 – 16 – 17 – 18 – 21 – 22 – 24 – 25.

Para jogar na Lotofácil, é preciso escolher entre 15 e 20 números entre os 25 disponíveis no volante. A aposta com 15 números custa R$ 3,50, e o valor aumenta conforme a quantidade de dezenas marcadas, assim como a chance de acertar.

Também é possível optar pela Surpresinha, modalidade em que o sistema da Caixa Econômica Federal, responsável pela loteria, escolhe os números automaticamente.

São premiadas as apostas que acertam 11, 12, 13, 14 ou 15 números.

articles.title: Prefeito eleito em Martinópolis promete tapar buracos das vias e renegociação de dívidas | G1
articles.standfirst: Beto Leite (União Brasil) foi eleito neste domingo (25), em votação suplementar, com 59,09% dos votos válidos. Posse está prevista para 26 de novembro.
articles.summary: Beto Leite (União Brasil) foi eleito prefeito de Martinópolis (SP) neste domingo (25) com 59,09% dos votos válidos. Ele promete ações de tapa-buracos e renegociação de dívidas.
articles.body:
Eleito com 59,09% dos votos na eleição suplementar deste domingo (25), o novo prefeito de Martinópolis (SP), Humberto Emmanuel Schmidt Oliveira ( União Brasil ), conhecido como Beto Leite, afirmou que pretende iniciar a gestão com ações emergenciais para recuperar o asfalto da cidade e medidas para renegociar dívidas de água dos moradores.

A nova votação na cidade foi convocada após a cassação, em março deste ano, dos mandatos do prefeito Valdeci Soares dos Santos Filho (Republicanos) e do vice-prefeito Marcos Rogério Matarazo (Podemos), eleitos em 2024.

A defesa dos representantes recorreu da decisão, mas os recursos foram negados pelo Regional Eleitoral de São Paulo (TRE-SP) em junho deste ano.

Diante disso, o presidente da Câmara Municipal de Martinópolis (SP), Gabriel Valões Santos (MDB), assumiu temporariamente o cargo do Executivo desde então. Gabriel tentou se eleger como prefeito na eleição suplementar , mas não garantiu votos suficientes.

Em entrevista à TV TEM , o prefeito eleito, Beto Leite, destacou a infraestrutura como uma das prioridades da administração. A posse está prevista para 26 de novembro.

Entre os problemas enfrentados pelo município, Beto citou os buracos nas ruas, a necessidade de obras de infraestrutura e a inadimplência nas contas de água, que ultrapassou R$ 16 milhões em 2025.

Segundo o prefeito eleito, a primeira medida para melhorar as condições do asfalto será uma operação emergencial de tapa-buracos. Em seguida, a administração pretende elaborar um plano para buscar recursos estaduais e federais e viabilizar obras de maior porte.

"A questão do asfalto, nós vamos fazer um plano na cidade. Primeiro um tapa-buraco emergencial, depois vamos fazer um plano para buscar recursos em Brasília e em São Paulo para podermos fazer uma ação mais efetiva ao longo dos próximos dois anos", afirmou.

Prefeito eleito de Martinópolis (SP) promete tapa-buracos emergencial e renegociação de dívidas — Foto: Aceituno Jr./TV TEM

Beto Leite também destacou a necessidade de reorganizar a administração municipal e definir prioridades para os investimentos. Entre as obras citadas estão intervenções na Rua José Teodoro e na estação de tratamento do município.

Motoristas e pedestres de Martinópolis enfrentam dificuldades para circular pelas ruas da cidade devido à quantidade de buracos nas vias.

A situação se agravou após as chuvas do início deste ano e já provocou acidentes, como o de um carro que ficou com a roda presa em uma cratera nas proximidades de uma escola estadual.

Outro problema envolve uma obra na Rua José Teodoro. Em setembro deste ano, moradores pediram uma avaliação das condições de segurança do local, que apresentava trechos com asfalto rompido, barro, água acumulada e materiais soltos próximos aos acessos de imóveis.

A prefeitura anunciou o início dos trabalhos em 30 de junho de 2026 e, em agosto, informou que a previsão de conclusão era de 90 dias.

Questionado sobre as intervenções, Beto afirmou que pretende reorganizar a estrutura administrativa e o maquinário disponível para atender às demandas.

“A gente vai reorganizar a gestão de uma forma que possamos passar a trabalhar e cuidar dos principais problemas da cidade. Realmente é uma área asfáltica e a infraestrutura, tanto a José Teodoro quanto a estação de tratamento do município, são problemas que vão ser prioritariamente tratados”, disse.

O prefeito eleito reconheceu que o orçamento municipal é limitado e apontou a reorganização da frota e dos equipamentos públicos como parte das medidas necessárias para enfrentar os problemas.

Outro desafio para a nova administração será a inadimplência relacionada ao abastecimento de água. No ano passado, as contas atrasadas ultrapassaram os R$ 16 milhões em Martinópolis.

A prefeitura também chegou a registrar boletins de ocorrência por violações de cavaletes, equipamentos utilizados para medir o consumo de água. As adulterações levantaram suspeitas de ligações clandestinas, conhecidas como "gatos".

Durante a entrevista, Beto Leite afirmou que pretende discutir com a Câmara Municipal uma proposta para facilitar a regularização dos débitos.

“Nós vamos discutir um benefício. É a primeira condição, para as pessoas que pagarem, excluir os juros de correção. E com isso, nós vamos retomar a dimensão e vamos passar a cuidar, para que as pessoas se mantenham em direção ao desconto de água, que vai ser bom para o município“, explicou.

Antes da posse, Beto Leite diz que pretende iniciar conversas com os diferentes setores da prefeitura para organizar a transição administrativa.

O prefeito eleito afirmou que pretende priorizar a estrutura de trabalho dos servidores e a reorganização dos equipamentos municipais.

A diplomação de Beto Leite e da vice-prefeita eleita, Fernanda Xavier Passos Crepaldi (União Brasil), está prevista para 19 de novembro. A posse deve ocorrer em 26 de novembro, conforme divulgado pelo Cartório Eleitoral.

articles.title: Ponte de pedestres sobre córrego cede e será interditada em Campinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura no Jardim do Lago cedeu e interrompeu a travessia entre duas ruas do bairro; prefeitura prevê manutenção em até 30 dias.
articles.summary: Estrutura no Jardim do Lago cedeu e interrompeu a travessia entre duas ruas do bairro; prefeitura prevê manutenção em até 30 dias.
articles.body:
Parte de uma ponte de pedestres cedeu e interrompeu a travessia no Jardim do Lago, em Campinas (SP). Imagens registradas por um morador mostram um homem tentando atravessar a estrutura, mas impedido pelo desabamento de um trecho da passagem sobre um córrego do bairro.

A ponte liga as ruas Mestre Tom Jobim e Rev. Prof. Herculano Gouvêia Júnior e é utilizada por moradores para a circulação entre os dois lados do córrego.

Procurada pela EPTV, afiliada da TV Globo, a Prefeitura de Campinas informou que irá interditar o local e que a manutenção da estrutura deve ser realizada em até 30 dias corridos.

articles.title: Resultado Quina 7152: duas apostas de MT ganham R$ 4,3 mil na Quina | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogos feitos em Cuiabá e Várzea Grande acertaram quatro números no sorteio desta segunda-feira (26). Não houve ganhadores na faixa principal.
articles.summary: Jogos feitos em Cuiabá e Várzea Grande acertaram quatro números no sorteio desta segunda-feira (26). Não houve ganhadores na faixa principal.
articles.body:
Canhoto da Quina sem preenchimento — Foto: Augusto Castro

Duas apostas feitas em Cuiabá e Várzea Grande , em Mato Grosso, acertaram quatro dos cinco números sorteados no concurso 7152 da Quina , realizado nesta segunda-feira (26). Cada aposta ganhou R$ 4.321,22.

As duas apostas foram simples, com cinco números marcados.

Em todo o país, 61 apostas acertaram quatro números e ganharam prêmios de R$ 4.321,22 cada. Ninguém acertou os cinco números, e o prêmio principal acumulou.

articles.title: Governo Trump acusa novamente ex-diretor do FBI James Comey | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova acusação foi anunciada nesta segunda-feira (26), no mesmo dia em que um juiz considerou ilegal a demissão de Maurene Comey, filha do ex-diretor, do cargo de promotora federal.
articles.summary: James Comey já responde a processos por mentir ao Congresso e por supostamente ameaçar Trump. Em decisão separada, juiz considerou ilegal a demissão de sua filha.
articles.body:
O ex-diretor do FBI James Comey fala com jornalistas no Capitólio, em Washington, D.C., em 17 de dezembro de 2018. — Foto: AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, arquivo

O ex-diretor do FBI James Comey foi acusado novamente pelo Departamento de Justiça dos Estados Unidos , segundo a NBC News. O novo processo ocorre no momento em que um juiz federal decidiu que a demissão de sua filha, Maurene Comey, do cargo de promotora federal pelo governo de Donald Trump foi ilegal.

Em um vídeo publicado no Instagram, James Comey afirmou que as autoridades voltaram a agir contra ele e declarou que é inocente. Ele não deu detalhes sobre a nova acusação.

Comey já responde a outros processos federais.

No ano passado, foi acusado de mentir ao Congresso sobre a autorização de vazamentos de informações à imprensa. O caso foi arquivado depois que um juiz concluiu que o promotor responsável pela acusação não havia sido nomeado legalmente.

Em outro processo, o ex-diretor do FBI foi acusado de ameaçar Trump após publicar uma fotografia de conchas organizadas para formar os números “86 47”. A combinação foi interpretada como uma possível referência à retirada do presidente do cargo. Comey se declarou inocente das acusações.

Trump demitiu Comey do comando do FBI em 2017 , durante seu primeiro mandato, quando a agência investigava contatos entre a campanha presidencial republicana de 2016 e russos. Desde então, o ex-diretor se tornou um crítico do presidente.

Juiz considera ilegal demissão da filha de Comey

No mesmo dia, a filha do ex-diretor, Maurene Comey, teve sua demissão tida como ilegal. Ela atuou como promotora no escritório do procurador federal de Manhattan desde 2015 e participou de processos criminais contra Ghislaine Maxwell, associada de Jeffrey Epstein, e o magnata da música Sean “Diddy” Combs.

Maurene foi demitida pelo Departamento de Justiça em julho de 2025, poucos meses após o início do segundo mandato de Trump. Na ação judicial, ela argumentou que perdeu o cargo por ser filha de James Comey, em violação às normas que protegem servidores federais contra demissões por motivos políticos.

O juiz federal Jesse Furman determinou nesta segunda que ela fosse reintegrada retroativamente ao cargo até dezembro de 2025, o que permite o pagamento de salários atrasados e o acesso a benefícios de aposentadoria.

O Departamento de Justiça afirmou que discorda da decisão e pretende recorrer.

articles.title: Comissária de bordo é homenageada em voo ao retornar pela 1ª vez ao AC | G1
articles.standfirst: Glenda Leite deixou o Acre em 2020 e integra quadro de companhia aérea. Nesta segunda-feira (26), viagem na qual ela trabalhou chegou à capital acreana e marcou o reencontro com a família.
articles.summary: Glenda Leite deixou o Acre em 2020 e integra quadro de companhia aérea. Nesta segunda-feira (26), viagem na qual ela trabalhou chegou à capital acreana e marcou o reencontro.
articles.body:
🛬❤️ O trem de pouso tocou o solo e a aeronave desacelerou até parar na pista do Aeroporto Internacional de Rio Branco . Porém, o frio na barriga começou neste momento para a comissária de bordo Glenda Pinheiro Batista Leite. Ela retornou pela primeira vez ao Acre após seis anos de carreira em um voo que chegou à capital na manhã desta segunda-feira (26).

Se a volta para casa, ainda que temporária, já não fosse emocionante o suficiente, ela foi surpreendida por uma homenagem de sua família ainda dentro da aeronave. Uma mensagem carinhosa foi lida por uma colega tripulante e transmitiu o afeto daqueles que mais torcem por sua carreira enquanto ela era aplaudida pelos ocupantes. (Veja vídeo acima)

“Aquela menina que cresceu numa casa simples, tantas vezes atingida pelas enchentes, hoje realiza o sonho de voar e conquista os céus do Brasil. Glenda, hoje você não está apenas chegando a Rio Branco, está voltando para casa, levando consigo uma linda história de coragem, superação e vitória. [...] Esta homenagem é da sua mãe, seus irmãos, seus cunhados, seus primos e toda a tripulação, que te ama e sente muito orgulho de você. Uma acreana voando alto, disse parte da homenagem.

Glenda, família e colegas de tripulação registraram encontro em Rio Branco — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Glenda contava os dias para rever sua família, mas não imaginava que fosse receber este gesto de carinho. A mãe dela, os irmãos, cunhadas e um sobrinho estavam presentes na chegada.

“Foi bem bonito, os comissários fizeram essa homenagem, minha família estava me esperando no aeroporto, estouraram confetes para mim. Estava todo mundo muito feliz. Foi bem emocionante mesmo, porque todo mundo que estava eram os que estavam torcendo e foram as pessoas que me ajudaram, tanto financeiramente como emocionalmente”, contou ao g1 .

Glenda Pinheiro Batista Leite deixou o Acre há seis anos para se tornar comissária de bordo — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Mais do que a oportunidade de rever a família em sua cidade natal, a recepção especial trouxe a Glenda memórias e reflexões sobre sua trajetória. Sua mãe era cobradora de ônibus e trabalhava em uma linha que chegava ao aeroporto.

Foi a partir daí que ela participou de um processo seletivo para menor aprendiz em uma companhia aérea, e foi selecionada. Após o período de aprendizado ela foi efetivada, e nunca mais deixou o setor.

“Trabalhei como agente de aeroporto por algum tempo em Rio Branco, logo em seguida eu saí, e em 2020 fui embora para fazer o curso de comissário de bordo em Fortaleza . Aqui o valor era um pouco alto, e a gente também não tinha tantas condições. A gente encontrou essa escola em Fortaleza, e minha família me apoiou. Minha mãe foi embora comigo, eu fui fazer o curso, formei, daí eu casei, e fui morar em Campina Grande , na Paraíba”, lembrou.

Ela já tem hora marcada para ir embora: às 9h desta terça (27). Enquanto isso, aproveita o tempo, ainda que curto, para amenizar a saudade da família.

“Passa um filme na cabeça da pessoa, né? Porque é toda uma realidade. Eu vim de família humilde, a gente morava no [bairro] Habitasa, e a gente sempre imaginava que a gente ia conquistar certas coisas. Quando a gente vê, que eu vim, trabalhando, trazendo os acreanos no voo, é muito gratificante”, finalizou.

articles.title: 7-year-old Skyler Rozell-Whitaker wore 50 sweaters at once to break a Guinness World Record, then donated them all to charity
articles.summary: Seven-year-old Skyler Rozell-Whitaker from the United States wore 50 sweaters at once to claim the world record for the most jumpers or sweaters worn at
articles.body: Seven-year-old Skyler Rozell-Whitaker from the United States wore 50 sweaters at once to claim the world record for the most jumpers or sweaters worn at once. The second grader beat the previous mark of 46, held by fellow American Hanmisha Voddineni, by adding four more layers during an attempt on 1 June that was cheered on by classmates, friends and family. Now eight, Skyler has handed every single sweater to a local clothing drive, turning an official record attempt into a gift for his community. The attempt took place in Pennsylvania and drew television coverage as far away as Australia.Why a young boy chose sweaters: The long-held wish for a world record and a habit of givingSkyler has always wanted to hold a world record, according to Guinness World Records, but it took time to find a challenge that suited his age and reflected his passion for helping others. He volunteers with his family every quarter at a local clothing drive, so a title built around clothes offered a way to combine both interests in a single attempt.How a trial run and secondhand shops got him ready for a record sweater attemptBefore the big day, Skyler and his mothers ran a trial to check that the garments layered properly and that he did not become too hot or overwhelmed. They gathered dozens of sweaters from local secondhand shops and topped up the pile with brand-new items from Walmart. Although it was summer, they practised indoors beside a fan to keep him cool. His mother, Patty Rozell-Whitaker, told the organisation that once the family knew he was safe, comfortable and happy, all that remained was folding and sorting the sweaters by size.Skyler disliked sweaters but kept calm through layer after layerThe challenge took place in the children’s room of the public library in Monroeville. As his mother helped pull each sweater over his head, Skyler stayed mentally and physically cool, despite a genuine dislike of wearing them. He explained that sweaters feel itchy and that, as a sensory child, he avoids clothes that do not feel comfortable. When the final sweater went on, its black hem tugged over the bulky pile; he looked joyful. Friends hugged him afterwards, but, as Skyler told Guinness World Records, “I couldn’t move my arms to hug back.” His favourite moment was taking the sweaters off, because the weight around his neck felt strange.From parkour belts to a bicycle attempt, what he wants to try nextSkyler says he has been bitten by the record-breaking bug. In October, he plans to help his mother with another attempt involving a bicycle, and he is working on helping his elementary school and his best friend Liam earn titles of their own. Alongside the plans, he stays busy with school, parkour and karate, where he has reached orange belt, and with playing alongside friends and pets.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Looked so corrupt’: Trump questions Brazil election after Lula defeats his ally
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump claimed Brazil’s presidential election looked “rigged” and “so corrupt” after incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated his
articles.body: US president Donald Trump claimed Brazil’s presidential election looked “rigged” and “so corrupt” after incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated his right-wing ally Flávio Bolsonaro, raising questions over how Washington will respond to the result.Trump, speaking to reporters as he left Washington for a campaign rally ahead of next week’s US midterm elections, criticised the counting process and a last-minute decision to extend voting hours across Brazil.“It looked like another rigged election, frankly,” Trump said. “It was a terrible look for the world.”Asked whether he would take any action over the result, Trump declined to commit to a response, saying he was focused on domestic politics.“I’m not running for Brazil, I’m running for the USA,” he said. “I like Lula, I get along with him very well. I just thought it was a very bad look, the way it was tabulated — with the extension.”Trump did not provide evidence to support his claims of irregularities. His remarks came after Flávio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, called for the runoff result to be annulled. The challenge is considered unlikely to overturn Lula’s victory.Voting extension becomes focus of criticismBrazil’s Supreme Court ordered voting to be extended nationwide by two hours on Sunday after both candidates sought additional time in some areas. Lula’s request followed problems involving buses transporting voters in nine states, while Bolsonaro cited heavy rain in southern Brazil.The extension caused confusion at some polling stations, with reports that voting machines had already been switched off before officials received the order to keep voting open.Trump described the extension as “very strange” and cited it as a reason the election had a “very bad look”. However, he did not present evidence that the decision or the vote count had altered the outcome.Flávio Bolsonaro’s demand to annul the result echoes efforts by his father to challenge his defeat in Brazil’s previous presidential election. Jair Bolsonaro was later convicted of plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in an attempt to overturn the result.Trump’s Latin America ambitions face a setbackTrump’s comments come as he has repeatedly claimed credit for a rightward shift in Latin American politics, pointing to victories by conservative allies across the region. Brazil’s result leaves the country under Lula, a veteran left-wing leader whose government has clashed with Washington over trade and security policy.“In South America, it was all leaning big left — it’s all right now,” Trump told reporters last week, claiming that every candidate he had endorsed in the region had won.He described the shift towards conservative leadership as “extremely conservative in a very positive way”.An ally of the Bolsonaro family, Trump had backed a political direction for Brazil that would bring it closer to his administration. Flávio Bolsonaro had promised to improve ties with Washington and pursue better deals with the US, including in the strategic minerals sector.Despite the political divide, Trump has also spoken warmly of Lula. The two leaders have previously described their personal exchanges positively despite tensions over tariffs and other policy disputes.Lula’s victory therefore leaves Washington facing a Brazilian government that has resisted some of Trump’s economic and diplomatic pressure, even as the US president says he maintains good personal relations with the Brazilian leader.You use AI every day. articles.title: First confirmed Ebola patient in Nigeria evacuated to Switzerland
articles.summary: A Swiss woman being treated for Ebola in Nigeria was medically evacuated to Switzerland with her husband Monday, officials said, as Nigerian authorities continued monitoring 52 people who had been in contact with her.
articles.body: A Swiss woman being treated for Ebola in Nigeria was medically evacuated to Switzerland with her husband Monday, officials said, as Nigerian authorities continued monitoring 52 people who had been in contact with her. Nigerian Health Minister Muhammad Pate said the woman, the country’s first case in the current outbreak, left the capital, Abuja, early Monday with his approval. Her condition had improved significantly, and she was stable, conscious and able to communicate, he said. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place,” Pate wrote on X. Her husband, a Swiss diplomat in Nigeria, has shown no symptoms. Switzerland’s Federal Office of Public Health said the couple arrived Monday on a medical evacuation flight. The woman was being treated at Geneva University Hospital, while her husband was in isolation at Zurich University Hospital. The agency said both hospitals were equipped to care for them and that there was no risk to the Swiss public. The World Health Organization’s regional director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said the evacuation was arranged because the couple are Swiss citizens and that Nigerian medical teams had stabilized the woman after treating her through the acute phase of the illness. Nigeria will continue monitoring 52 other contacts, Janabi said. “With the evacuation of the patient and her husband, Nigeria currently has no Ebola cases,” he said, stressing that vigilance remained critical. Pate said containment measures remained in place and urged Nigerians to remain vigilant. The woman tested positive after returning to Abuja from Uganda. Nigerian authorities said Friday they had yet to establish how she contracted the virus. Switzerland’s foreign ministry told The Associated Press that she had not visited Congo and was believed to have been infected while traveling to Uganda with her husband. The Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said the first patients in Nigeria and Kenya had both traveled through Uganda’s Entebbe International Airport on Oct. 3. Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases but later declared itself free of the virus. Kenya has recorded nine cases, including two deaths, since confirming its first case earlier this month. On Monday, Kenya released 20 people from quarantine following their exposure to the virus as contacts of the country’s first case, while 98 others were expected to be released starting next Tuesday. “Each of the 20 contacts was assessed against the release criteria, including 21 days without any symptoms since their last exposure,” the Kenyan Ministry of Health said in a statement. The spread of Ebola beyond Congo has heightened longstanding fears among health authorities about the rapid transmission of the rare Bundibugyo virus. The latest figures from Congo’s health ministry show more than 9,900 cases, including more than 4,800 deaths, since the outbreak began in May. WHO has said the outbreak is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record and is on track to surpass the death toll of the deadliest: West Africa’s 2014-16 outbreak, which killed 11,000 people. Nigeria was among the countries affected, recording 20 cases before its outbreak was declared over after three months.

articles.title: From Andamans to Zanskar, e-Sanjeevani bridges distances, posts 50cr consultations
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: High fever and laboured breathing threatened the life of Oho-Tahane, a child from Jarawa tribe of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: High fever and laboured breathing threatened the life of Oho-Tahane, a child from Jarawa tribe of Andaman and Nicobar Islands. With specialist care out of reach, health workers turned to e-Sanjeevani for remote consultation. The doctor diagnosed pneumonia, and timely expert intervention helped the child’s condition improve rapidly.Oho-Tahane, a member of one of India’s most vulnerable tribal groups, is among over 50 crore cases, many in far flung areas, facilitated by the national telemedicine service since its launch in Nov 2019.The service’s achievement was highlighted by PM Narendra Modi in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ address Sunday, as he also cited how e-Sanjeevani enabled a doctor to guide a medical team in treating Kunhi Koya (60) in Kalpeni, Lakshadweep, and helped ensure medical assistance for pregnant Kunjang Dolma in Himalayan region of Zanskar.Developed by C-DAC Mohali under the health ministry, e-Sanjeevani facilitates 2.5-3 lakh daily consultations, offers services in 15 languages and is available across all 36 states and UTs. Women account for 57.1% of the platform’s utilisation, while people aged 46 and above account for 40.1% of consultations. Those aged 60 and above account for 16.2%. The platform has recorded a peak of 6,30,315 consultations in a single day.Modi credited the platform’s reach to dedication of doctors, public trust and the effective use of technology. He highlighted 1.9 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, saying they were bringing healthcare closer to rural communities and evolving into wellness centres for village panchayats. Regular health check-ups were becoming more common in rural areas, he said, with e-Sanjeevani playing an important role.The PM also highlighted advances in brain research, referring to Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT-Madras, which he inaugurated this month. The centre has developed a brain imaging technology platform to create high resolution digital 3D images of human brain. Its mission is to map and study 100 human brains in detail using Param Shakti supercomputer..Modi said the initiative could deepen understanding of the brain, particularly as conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease and dementia lack a definitive cure. articles.title: Britain’s £210 million London mansion has 45 rooms and an indoor pool, yet a homeless former journalist has slept outside for 3 years
articles.summary: A London mansion that sold for £210 million in 2020 has remained unoccupied inside for years, while a homeless former journalist has made its covered
articles.body: A London mansion that sold for £210 million in 2020 has remained unoccupied inside for years, while a homeless former journalist has made its covered entrance his shelter. Located at 2-8A Rutland Gate in Knightsbridge, the property has 45 rooms, 4 lifts, an indoor swimming pool and 116 windows, 68 of which overlook Hyde Park. Anders Fernstedt, a Swedish-born former journalist, has lived on its porch for about 3 years, sleeping beneath a makeshift tent made largely from umbrellas. His belongings include books, flowers, baskets, pictures and teddy bears. In a June 2026 report, The Guardian documented Fernstedt’s life outside the mansion and the property’s complicated ownership history. The contrast between the vacant interior and the makeshift shelter outside has drawn attention to the intersection of luxury property and homelessness in London.Why Britain’s £210 million mansion remains emptyThe present building at 2-8 Rutland Gate dates from 1985–87 and was designed by the architectural firm YRM. Westminster’s 2021 planning report says it replaced earlier buildings on the site and was designed to mimic the architectural style of the 1860s. A later proposal to convert the property into 13 flats was never implemented. A certificate issued in 2019 confirmed that the building had been used as a single-family dwelling for more than 4 years. The site was acquired in the early 1980s by interests associated with Lebanese billionaire Rafik Hariri, who later became prime minister of Lebanon. The present building was constructed in 1985–87 and became associated with Hariri as his London residence. He was assassinated in Beirut in 2005. According to The Guardian, the property was then given to Sultan bin Abdulaziz, the crown prince of Saudi Arabia, who died in 2011. The mansion’s contents, including ornate bathroom fittings, chandeliers and gold-leaf wastepaper bins, were auctioned in 2015.The property changed hands in 2020 for a reported £210 million, making it Britain’s most expensive house at the time. The purchase was publicly associated with Cheung Chung-kiu, the Hong Kong-based chairman of CC Land Holdings. However, The Guardian, citing earlier Financial Times reporting, identified Hui Ka Yan, founder of Chinese property developer Evergrande, as the ultimate owner. The house was put on the market again in 2022 for a reported £200 million but did not sell. Land Registry information cited by The Guardian identifies Vision Perfect Global Limited, a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, as the purchasing vehicle in 2020. Following changes to transparency rules, Hui’s then-wife, Ding Yumei, was named as the company’s ultimate beneficial owner. The couple have since divorced.Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prisonThe property’s ownership story took another turn on August 20, 2026, when a court in Shenzhen sentenced Hui Ka Yan to life imprisonment for financial crimes connected to Evergrande’s collapse. The court also imposed substantial fines on the company and related entities. Hui had pleaded guilty in April to charges including fraud and illegally taking public deposits, according to The Associated Press. Evergrande, once one of China’s largest property developers, defaulted on its debts in 2021. Its liabilities exceeded $300 billion, and its collapse became a major episode in China’s prolonged property-sector crisis.The sentence does not establish that the London mansion itself has been confiscated or transferred. In its June 2026 report, The Guardian said Evergrande’s liquidators could not seize the property because of the ownership arrangements involving Ding Yumei. It also reported that her assets had been frozen, leaving the property’s future uncertain. The last change of ownership identified in the Land Registry information cited by The Guardian was the 2020 transaction. No later transfer is established in the sources used for this article.Who is Anders Fernstedt, the former journalist living outside the mansion?Fernstedt was born in Sweden in 1968 and worked as a journalist, writing technology articles for business publications. He later developed an interest in horticulture and enrolled at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh in 2009 to study horticulture and plantsmanship, according to The Guardian. He subsequently worked briefly as a freelance fact-checker for The Economist. He also lived on a small sailboat in Essex and commuted to London for work. His freelance commissions eventually dried up, leaving him without a regular income.In its June 2026 account, The Guardian described Fernstedt’s experiences of insecure work, repeated no-fault evictions and an assault that left him with a ruptured eardrum. While he was in hospital, his belongings were stolen from the corridor of the building where he had been living. He was left without his possessions or a place to go. Fernstedt began sleeping rough and eventually settled beneath the mansion’s covered entrance. A report published by Berliner Zeitung on October 19, 2026, said Fernstedt had never been inside the mansion. Instead, he has gradually arranged his belongings around the porch, using flowers and containers to create what he describes as a pretend garden. His circumstances illustrate how homelessness can follow a series of setbacks involving work, housing insecurity and personal safety. His education and professional experience did not protect him from eventually sleeping outside.Rough sleeping in England reaches a record highThe circumstances at Rutland Gate sit within a wider housing crisis. The UK government’s Rough sleeping snapshot in England: autumn 2025, published on February 26, 2026, estimated that 4,793 people were sleeping rough in England on a single night. This was the highest figure recorded under the current snapshot system. The estimate was 3% higher than in 2024 and 171% above the 2010 figure, when the current methodology was introduced. London recorded an estimated 1,277 people sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025, a 3% decrease from the previous year. Westminster remained the local authority with the highest estimated number, at 360 people.The government’s snapshot is a one-night estimate, not a count of everyone who experiences homelessness during the year. It does not capture the full range of housing insecurity, including people staying temporarily with friends or family or living in temporary accommodation. The government also cautions that rough sleeping among women can be less visible and may not be fully captured by the method used. At Rutland Gate, the contrast is specific: a mansion sold for £210 million in 2020 remains unoccupied inside, while a former journalist has spent years living beneath its entrance. Hui’s sentencing has added another development to the property’s complicated ownership story, but the mansion’s eventual future remains unresolved. articles.title: Africa food security under threat due to Iran war, trade officials warn
articles.summary: The war on Iran is driving up fuel and fertiliser costs across Africa, threatening food security, trade officials say.
articles.body:
Doha, Qatar – African countries are feeling the economic fallout from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, with rising fuel and fertiliser prices threatening to drive up food costs, according to trade ministers from the region and the United Nations’ top trade official.

The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz due to the United States and Israel’s war on Iran needs to be resolved “sooner rather than later”, Luz Maria de la Mora, director of the Division on International Trade and Commodities at UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD), told Al Jazeera at the World Investment Forum on Monday. She warned that soaring fertiliser prices could affect harvests next year.

“Prices of fertilisers have risen dramatically … so many countries have decided to reduce the use of fertilisers, which will have an effect next year in terms of crops,” she said.

“It may have an effect on availability of food and prices of food.”

The US-Israel war on Iran has highlighted the world’s heavy reliance on the strategic waterway , through which one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade previously passed.

Against this backdrop, Doha hosted UNCTAD’s World Investment Forum on October 25 and 26, bringing together heads of state, policymakers, CEOs and investors to discuss global investment and sustainable development.

The Strait of Hormuz’s disruption has rippled through African economies. In Zimbabwe, rising fuel and fertiliser prices are a critical concern in a country where more than 70 percent of the population depends on agriculture, Monica Mutsvangwa, the country’s minister of women affairs, community, small and medium enterprise development, told Al Jazeera.

Uganda, another heavily agrarian economy, has also been hit, with fuel prices more than doubling, Sanjay Tanna, the country’s minister of trade, industry and cooperatives, told Al Jazeera.

The impact extends beyond the immediate cost of energy. Rising oil prices have disrupted supply chains, with effects lasting longer than anticipated, according to de la Mora.

“The effects are lasting longer than we would have expected or would have wanted,” she said.

The shock has also exposed differences in how African economies weather global disruption.

Uganda’s reliance on subsistence farming has helped cushion the impact, with domestic food production offering some protection from international market volatility, said Tanna.

But the country has not been insulated from financial pressures: its currency has lost 10 percent of its value against the US dollar, the minister said. The Ugandan shilling has steadily declined since mid-2026.

For Zimbabwe, the crisis has reinforced the importance of attracting investment while maintaining economic ties across geopolitical divides.

Amid the simmering trade war between the US and China, Harare considers itself a potential partner to investors from either side, Mutsvangwa said.

“We are a friend to all and an enemy to none,” she said.

“Money has no color … If we get an investor who comes into our country, follows the rules and regulations of the country, makes his money, and Zimbabwe develops, that’s what we want.”

The official pointed to Zimbabwe’s deposits of more than 60 critical minerals, including lithium and graphite, as well as its tourism potential.

But attracting foreign capital remains a challenge for developing economies, with investment concentrated in a relatively small number of countries.

That concentration is “very understandable”, de la Mora said, arguing that investors need confidence that their money will generate returns.

“Capital is risk averse. Capital needs to have certainty that its investment is going to yield returns and it’s going to come to fruition,” she said.

Governments can help build that confidence through transparent institutions, the rule of law and investment in infrastructure, including reliable electricity, energy supplies and digital connectivity, she added.

The question of whether the international trading system treats all countries equally prompted a more blunt assessment from Uganda’s trade minister.

“Of course not,” said Tanna. “The world cannot be equal … It’s unfair, but we believe that, within the space that we are in, we are in a good space.”

Uganda was well placed for the future, he argued, because it produces its own food – an advantage at a time when international supply chains are under pressure.

For both Uganda and the Republic of Congo, building resilient economies also means investing in younger generations.

The Republic of Congo’s Deputy Prime Minister for Coordination, Development Infrastructure and Land Planning, Jean-Jacques Bouya, said the country had aligned its national development plan, Vision 2063, with the African Union’s broader development ambitions.

Connectivity – through electricity, digital infrastructure and physical links – is central to that strategy, he told Al Jazeera.

The Republic of Congo also wants to expand local processing so that more value from its natural resources remains within the country.

“Africa can no longer be a reservoir of raw materials, and neither can Congo – a place where raw materials are extracted, taken elsewhere, processed and then sold back to us at a much higher price. We cannot go on like this,” Bouya said.

articles.title: A cooling-off period for MPs, MLAs who quit? SC to decide
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a development that could impact politics of shifting loyalties, SC Monday agreed to examine whether an MLA or an MP who contests a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a development that could impact politics of shifting loyalties, SC Monday agreed to examine whether an MLA or an MP who contests a by-election caused by their voluntary resignation should be made to bear the entire expenses incurred by Election Commission in conducting the previous poll.Senior advocate Shoeb Alam told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that six persons elected on AIADMK tickets to the Tamil Nadu assembly had resigned in May and June after declaration of results and defected to TVK. Two of them resigned, causing by-elections which they went on to win, this time as TVK candidates.Appearing for petitioner K Suthan, Alam said the court was required to examine whether a person who voluntarily resigned as an MLA or MP should be barred for five years from contesting a state or parliamentary election. SC issued notices to Centre, EC and the six AIADMK MLAs who resigned and defected.The trend of lawmakers crossing over to the party in office and quitting their seats to avoid disqualification has caught on. The petitioner has sought legislative or regulatory measures “to create a mechanism for ensuring financial accountability of elected representatives who prematurely resign from their seats without legally recognised compelling circumstances, including introduction of an ‘Election Expenditure Security’ to recover cost of resultant bye-elections”.He has requested the court to direct Centre and EC to examine and initiate “necessary legislative and/or regulatory measures to introduce a statutory disqualification or a reasonable cooling-off period to prevent elected representatives who voluntarily and prematurely resign from contesting subsequent polls”. Suthan has suggested a five-year cooling-off period.The petitioner contended that none of the vacancies in the six seats was caused by death, permanent disability, disqualification or other compelling circumstance warranting a bypoll. “Public shouldn’t be made to pay twice for polls to the same constituency because of an individual’s personal or political choice to resign,” he said.Refusing to entertain Suthan’s petition, a Madras HC bench led by CJ S A Dharmadhikari had said, “We are being asked to design a punitive and financial regime that would operate as a fresh disqualification under Constitution and would curtail statutory right to contest election. In our opinion, the same is a matter of legislative policy, not of judicial direction.”“Right to resign a legislative seat is itself a facet of the constitutional scheme governing membership of a House and cannot be burdened with extra-statutory conditions by judicial order, however sound the underlying concern may be,” the HC had said while refusing the plea to impose a five-year cooling-off period on MPs and MLAs who voluntarily resign from their seats in the House concerned.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
articles.summary: Comey's lawyers say the case stems from alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in 2016.
articles.body:
Federal prosecutors have taken steps to charge ex-Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director James Comey with leaking national defence information, according to a court filing.

It marks the third time the justice department has moved to bring criminal charges against Comey, a longtime critic of President Donald Trump.

Few details are provided about the two counts in the three-page filing, but Comey's lawyers said in separate court papers that the case stemmed from an alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in October 2016, while he was head of the FBI.

Comey denied any wrongdoing in a video posted on Substack on Monday, calling the charges an "appalling abuse".

"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the department of justice, one that we cannot become numb to," he said in the clip.

"Nothing's changed with me - I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe the independent federal judiciary."

His lawyer, Patrick Fitzgerald, said in a statement that two different teams of prosecutors had investigated the alleged disclosure to the New York Times a decade ago during the first Trump administration.

"Both times the Government determined that no charges should be brought against anyone," he said.

The attorney said the court filing "purports to charge Mr Comey with crimes that he did not commit".

Comey was charged in Washington DC through a criminal information, which is a formal written charging document filed directly by a prosecutor.

This is different to a criminal indictment, which must be approved by a grand jury, a group of citizens sworn in to review if evidence is strong enough to prosecute.

Comey was fired by Trump during his first term, after the former FBI director opened an investigation into claims of Russian meddling in the US 2016 presidential election.

Since then, Trump has repeatedly called for his prosecution, and these charges are the administration's third attempt to do so.

Comey was first indicted by a federal grand jury in September 2025 on charges that he had lied to Congress during testimony and obstructed a congressional proceeding.

He pleaded not guilty the following month before the case was dismissed in November.

In April 2026, Comey surrendered to authorities to face charges alleging that an image he briefly shared on social media posed a threat to Trump's life.

The case stemmed from a 2025 Instagram post by Comey, which contained a photo of seashells on a beach arranged to read "86 47".

"Eighty-six" is a slang term for "get rid of", and prosecutors allege it encourages violence against Trump, the 47th president.

Comey denies any wrongdoing, saying he did not know what the numbers meant, and accusing the prosecution of political motivation. That case is ongoing.

articles.title: In 1898, Canada's Bennett City filled with thousands of gold seekers built boats for Dawson City; a year later, railway changed the Klondike gold rush route and the town's future
articles.summary: In the winter of 1897 and the spring that followed, the shores of Lake Bennett in north-western Canada filled with tents, timber and thousands of people
articles.body: In the winter of 1897 and the spring that followed, the shores of Lake Bennett in north-western Canada filled with tents, timber and thousands of people hoping to reach the Klondike goldfields. The settlement that grew there became a temporary centre of life for gold seekers who had crossed difficult mountain trails carrying food, equipment and whatever else they could manage. Some had spent months getting that far. Their next challenge was to build boats and wait for the ice to clear, allowing them to travel down the Yukon River towards Dawson City. The rush created a crowded settlement almost overnight, but its fortunes depended on a journey that was soon to change.How Bennett City became a crowded stopping point on the Klondike gold rush routeBennett occupied an important position on the route taken by people heading towards the Klondike. The settlement stood where Lake Bennett met the trails leading over the coastal mountains from Skagway, Alaska, and Dyea. One route crossed the White Pass; the other followed the Chilkoot Pass. Both demanded considerable physical effort, and travellers had to carry large quantities of provisions before they could continue into the Yukon interior.The people arriving at the lakes were not all experienced prospectors. Clerks, farmers, labourers and others who had left their ordinary lives behind found themselves in a landscape where even basic preparations took time. Many had hauled their supplies over steep, difficult ground, sometimes moving loads in several trips. Reaching Bennett did not mean the hardest part of the journey was over.During the winter of 1897–98, tents spread along the lake shore as the number of arrivals increased. The settlement became known as Bennett City, a temporary community whose population swelled with the arrival of each new group. Accounts of the period describe crowded camps at both Bennett and nearby Lake Lindeman, where people waited for the spring thaw.How 10,000 gold seekers built thousands of boats at Bennett CityFor many stampeders, the next task was to construct a boat. Carrying a finished vessel across the mountain passes was difficult, and some had decided to leave that option behind before setting out. Once they reached the lakes, they had to find timber, learn basic boatbuilding skills and put together something capable of surviving the journey downriver.By early spring 1898, roughly 10,000 gold seekers were camped along the shore of Lake Bennett, according to the Museum of History & Industry (MOHAI). They were waiting for the ice to clear while assembling supplies and building boats and scows for the journey towards the Klondike goldfields. The scale of the effort was considerable, with the US National Park Service recording that more than 7,000 boats were built during the winter of 1897–98.The work transformed the lakeside camps. Timber was cut from the surrounding forests, and men used long saws to turn logs into planks. A method known as whipsawing required two people to operate a saw from opposite sides of a log, with one working above and the other below. It was physically demanding work, particularly for people who had little previous experience with it.The demand for wood extended beyond boatbuilding. Campers needed fuel to cook and keep warm, as well as timber for temporary shelters and other structures. Photographs taken during the gold rush show tents and boats packed along the shoreline, with the surrounding landscape stripped of much of its accessible timber. The environmental effects of those months remained visible long after the crowds had gone.How the spring thaw sent thousands of stampeders towards Dawson CityThe camps were crowded, supplies had to be managed and news from home was difficult to obtain. Letters were particularly valuable to people who had travelled far from their families. Some relied on private carriers to transport their correspondence from Sheep Camp, where official US mail was delivered, to the settlements beside the lakes. A letter could cost 15 cents to bring the remaining distance, as reported by the Smithsonian National Postal Museum.By late May 1898, the long wait was ending. The Yukon River route could not be used safely until the ice began to break up, and rumours about conditions spread quickly through the camps. Some people set off too early and became caught in ice jams. Once the waterway was sufficiently clear, however, departures gathered pace.By the end of May, the river had opened enough for boats to begin leaving in large numbers. Hundreds set off each day, carrying people and the provisions they had spent months hauling across the mountains. For many, the prospect of finally moving towards Dawson City brought relief after a long winter spent building boats and waiting for the thaw.The railway reached Bennett City and changed its role in the gold rushConstruction of the White Pass and Yukon Route railway began in 1898, with the aim of creating a more direct transport link from the coastal port of Skagway into the Yukon. Building a railway through the steep mountain terrain was a major undertaking, but its arrival promised to remove much of the physical burden associated with hauling supplies over the passes.The railway reached Lake Bennett on 6 July 1899. For a short period, the town benefited from the new connection. Bennett became a transport point where passengers and freight could transfer between the railway and river services. Businesses serving travellers had a reason to remain, and the town experienced a fresh burst of activity.A growing railway network left the town behindBennett's short-lived prominence was tied to the period when people needed to cross the mountains, build boats and wait for the waterways to open. The railway altered that sequence. In 1900, the line reached Whitehorse, extending the railway connection farther into the Yukon before travellers transferred to river transport. Bennett and other settlements that had served as transfer points became less important.The railway's expansion coincided with a shift in the gold rush itself. Many of those who had travelled north in search of a fortune found that the most promising claims had already been taken. Some stayed to work for established miners or businesses, while others moved on in search of fresh opportunities. By 1899, the initial stampede was losing momentum, and new destinations were drawing people away from the original routes.What remains of Bennett's gold-rush yearsThe historical record offers a glimpse of a settlement that was both improvised and remarkably busy. Photographs show long rows of tents, boats gathered beside the water and people working in the cold to prepare for the journey ahead. Letters and diaries describe the uncertainty of waiting for mail, the difficulty of moving supplies and the anticipation surrounding the spring thaw.Those accounts also show how much effort went into reaching the goldfields. For many stampeders, the journey involved months of preparation and physical labour before they ever arrived in Dawson City. Bennett was the place where that effort paused, where boats were built and where people waited for conditions to allow them to move on.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Former FBI director James Comey hit with third set of charges under Trump
articles.summary: Comey, who was fired during Trump’s first term, has been accused of unlawfully divulging national security information.
articles.body:
James Comey, the former director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), is facing a third set of criminal charges under the administration of United States President Donald Trump.

On Monday, sealed documents came to light showing that the Trump administration has accused Comey of two counts related to the unlawful dissemination of “information related to national defence”.

Comey, a high-profile Trump critic, has not been indicted in the case. He has denied any wrongdoing.

But it is the third time the Trump administration has sought to level criminal charges against the former FBI director since the president returned to office in January 2025.

In an October court filing , prosecutors accuse Comey of ordering his FBI colleagues to leak information to the news media.

“The defendant [Comey] through one or more co-conspirators directed Individual #1 to disclose national defence information to a reporter for a national news publication,” the court filing reads.

In a video published on the online platform Substack, Comey once again denounced the Trump administration’s attempts to prosecute him as a campaign of political retribution.

“Well, now they’re back again. It would almost be funny if it weren’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice, one that we cannot become numb to,” Comey said.

“Nothing’s changed with me. I’m still innocent, and I’m still not afraid of these people, and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary.”

Comey also noted that Trump is only midway through his second term, and he hinted that he expects more criminal charges to come his way.

“The next couple years are going to be hard for all of us,” Comey added. “It’s really important that we stand straight and keep the faith in America.”

The latest charges pertain to a New York Times article from October 5, 2016, which describes how the email platform Yahoo was ordered to scan traffic on its site for a specific computer signature allegedly tied to a “terrorist” organisation.

Prosecutors have accused Comey of directing sensitive information to be disclosed to the reporter on that story, Charlie Savage.

In a statement released to news media, Comey’s defence lawyer Pat Fitzgerald framed the charges as feeble, claiming that the government had already investigated the matter twice before.

“Both times the Government determined that no charges should be brought against anyone,” the statement said.

Fitzgerald pointed out that government prosecutors had not sought an indictment, which involves presenting charges to a grand jury that must then choose whether to approve the criminal charges.

Instead, they are seeking to charge Comey through a process called a “criminal information”, which allows prosecutors to bypass a grand jury.

“Ten years after the article was published, the Government filed an ‘Information’ against Mr Comey that was not approved by a judge nor issued by a grand jury,” Fitzgerald said. “It purports to charge Mr Comey with crimes that he did not commit.”

Federal Judge Trevor McFadden, from the US District Court in Washington, DC, is overseeing the case. He is a Trump appointee.

Trump has long sought the prosecution of Comey, whom he fired from the role of FBI director in 2017, during his first term as president.

Comey had been FBI head since 2013. But his dismissal came as the FBI investigated the possibility of collusion between Russia and Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, a probe that Trump has repeatedly denounced as a “hoax”.

Following Trump’s second inauguration in 2025, his administration has sought the prosecution of several of the president’s critics, including Comey.

In September 2025, Trump appeared to request that then-Attorney General Pam Bondi look into Comey and other perceived political adversaries.

“Nothing is being done. What about Comey, Adam ‘Shifty’ Schiff, Leticia???” Trump wrote to Bondi in a social media post , referencing the former FBI director, a Democratic senator and New York Attorney General Letitia James. “They’re all guilty as hell, but nothing is going to be done.”

Trump concluded his post by telling Bondi not to “delay any longer” before pursuing the three critics.

“JUSTICE MUST BE SERVED, NOW,” he wrote.

Five days later, on September 25 of that year, Comey was indicted on charges of lying to Congress and obstructing a legislative proceeding.

The case was ultimately dismissed on the basis that the prosecutor in charge, Lindsey Halligan, was unlawfully appointed.

A second indictment came on April 28. In that case, the Trump administration accused Comey of threatening the president by posting a photo on social media of seashells, arranged to form the message “86 47”.

Forty-seven is a reference to Trump, the 47th president, and “86” is a rhyming word for “nix”, common in the service industry as code for throwing out a dish or customer.

The Trump administration, however, has argued that “86” implies violence. That case is ongoing.

Earlier on Monday, before the third set of charges was revealed, a federal judge in a separate case ruled that Comey’s daughter, former assistant US attorney Maurene Comey, had been unlawfully fired last year under Trump’s second term.

The younger Comey has maintained her termination was retaliation against her father. The court determined she was entitled to “retroactive reinstatement” and backpay.

James Comey has denied all accusations of criminal wrongdoing, and his legal team has sought to have the latest set of charges dismissed.

articles.title: Busted's James Bourne says 'hero' brother saved his life with kidney donation
articles.summary: The guitarist says doctors had given him "a few years left to live", but is now recovering well.
articles.body:
Busted star James Bourne has said his brother "saved my life" by donating a kidney, after doctors had given him "a few years left to live".

The guitarist, 43, dropped out of an arena tour featuring his band and fellow punk-pop favourites McFly in September 2025, just a day before it began.

He blamed health problems and was replaced by his younger brother Chris.

James later said he needed major surgery to "extend my life", and has now thanked his "hero" Chris and said they are both recovering from their transplant operations.

"Wow, what the hell happened?" James wrote on Monday. "One minute you're heading out on tour, the next thing you know you're on the bench and out of the game.

"My condition was serious and the doctors told me I had a few years left to live.

"I'm happy to share now that my youngest brother, Chris, who stepped in for me on tour last year, has saved my life yet again. This time quite literally by donating me one of his kidneys."

James continued: "I can't believe how much better I'm starting to feel already.

"I'm still going to need some time, but I wanted you to know that we're both recovering from surgery just fine. My brother is a hero."

Chris posted his own message on X saying simply: "We did it brother."

Bourne has not given any more details of his condition.

The guitarist, vocalist and songwriter shot to fame with Charlie Simpson and Matt Willis in Busted in the early 2000s, and the trio had hits including What I Go To School For, Year 3000 and Crashed the Wedding.

They scored four number one singles in the UK before splitting up in 2005. In 2013, Bourne and Willis teamed up with McFly to make McBusted, before Simpson rejoined Busted for a full reunion in 2015.

Bourne has written songs for McFly and 5 Seconds of Summer, and also fronted his own band, Son of Dork. He recently released the music from his stage musical Murder at the Gates.
